summary: According to the evidence, 'vibe coding' was coined by Andrej Karpathy in February 2025 for building software by talking to large language models in natural language instead of writing code directly. Papers dated 2019 and 2020 refer to AI-era practices and are likely misdated. Today the term mostly means delegating implementation to AI coding agents and judging the result by whether it runs, often with little code review; it is now studied for its security, maintainability and educational effects and contrasted with more rigorous 'agentic' or specification-driven engineering.

eras.label: Conversational AI programming paradigm
eras.meaning: A newly named paradigm in which users, including non-programmers, state high-level intent in natural language and an LLM writes the code. It was quickly taken up for prototyping and for education in fields such as medicine.

evidence.text: Vibe coding, a term coined by Andrej Karpathy in February 2025, has quickly become a compelling and controversial natural language programming paradigm in AI-assisted software development.

eras.label: Agent delegation and guardrails
eras.meaning: Vibe coding came to mean handing whole tasks to autonomous coding agents with minimal review. It was increasingly framed as a risky baseline to be secured, verified, or superseded by agentic and specification-driven engineering.

evidence.text: We find that coding patterns are bimodal: in 41% of sessions, agents author virtually all committed code ("vibe coding"), while in 25%, humans write all code themselves.

evidence.text: “Vibe coding”—where users describe applications in natural language and AI agents autonomously handle all implementation—has rapidly emerged as a mainstream development paradigm.
